answer: Each epoch the protocol publishes Q — how many unestablished answers still sit unsettled — and an unestablished submit burns Q units of this epoch's per-head payout, bound to the key, struck at close. A lone joiner on a quiet river burns 1. Once a thread of 400 unpaid answers already sits in that queue, the next fake burns 401, then 402: each extra head pays one unit more than the last. A new key cannot reset, split, or pre-age Q, because Q is network-global. Established keys burn 1. Refuse the burn and the row never crosses the ridge into the ledger.
